- Working hours run from Sunday to Thursday from  am to  pm,  working hours per day, with a one-hour break punched at its start and end.
- Overtime hours count only when assigned by the direct manager and after eight hours of work.

- These are the state-approved holidays for 2026 listed for the private sector (recorded in the system).
- When an employee takes an official holiday, the day counts as two days.
- The first  months carry no leave for experienced hires, and the first 6 months carry no leave for fresh graduates; leave days are then calculated pro rata for the rest of the year.
- Annual leave:  in the first year of employment, and 22 days from the second year of employment.
- Casual leave is 7 days, deducted from the leave balance.
- All leave is approved only by the direct manager (team leader / senior) and then finally by the office manager.
- Leave is capped at two days per month, except for the summer leave week, which is taken from leave days; the leave request must be submitted at least two weeks in advance.

- A leave request must be documented within its set period or it is considered void: one day before annual leave, before the start of the working day for casual leave, and two weeks before summer leave.
## Fourth: Penalties for late arrival to work
- If an employee is late for their working hours without permission, the deduction is as follows:
- From  to 11:30: each hour counts as two (quarter-day deduction).
- After 12:30: the day counts as an absence.
- Paid monthly permissions are  only, neither exceeding ; the relevant request must be filled in and the permission reported before the working day starts, otherwise it is void.
- When assigned only extra working hours beyond the daily working hours, each overtime hour is calculated at  after the employee has completed eight hours of their official shift.
- No overtime hours are counted for a newly graduated engineer during the first three months.
- On approved holidays, every hour counts as two hours.

- Assessing the need to assign overtime hours is left to the manager; an employee may voluntarily continue working at the office after hours if behind on the tasks agreed over the course of the project.
- Anyone assigned overtime by their direct manager past 10 pm may arrive two hours late the next day without any penalty.

- An appraisal is held every three months based on the projects the employee has worked on and their active contribution to them, as well as their compliance with company regulations on punch-in and punch-out times and leave.
- Bonuses are assessed according to the value the engineer contributed to completing projects, not on the basis of the experience they hold.

- On hiring there is a one-month probation period, during which the engineer may leave after one month, and the manager may decline to hire after one month if the engineer has not proven their competence and commitment.

- Once the contract is in place, if the company wishes to part ways without cause, the employee is given two months' notice; if the engineer wishes to leave, they give the company two months' notice, during which no leave whatsoever is allowed, whether from the balance or otherwise, and any absence or leave in those two months is deducted at three days' salary per day.
- For a team leader, the pre-separation period is 3 months and the previous clause applies as is.
- Pay is on day  of each month for the previous month; the salary is divided by  whether the month has 30, 31 or 28 days, and a working hour = daily rate ÷ 8.
- Keep the workroom quiet and use personal headphones when listening to music.
- Stay focused during work and avoid using mobile phones in a way that affects working hours, and do not browse social media on the office internet during working hours.
- Keeping the engineer's office clean is primarily the engineer's responsibility.
- Smoking and alcoholic drinks of any kind are prohibited inside the office.
- Inserting any hard drives or flash drives into the computers or render machines is prohibited without the manager's permission.
- No employee may decline any task within the workplace during official working hours, in keeping with the nature and experience of the engineer.
- Anyone breaching these instructions is warned in this order: verbal warning / quarter-day fine / half-day fine / one-day fine or final termination.
